## Boundary and contract observations

`--profile` is required and argparse rejects unknown values before server startup; both were exercised. Registration uses the selected profile's tool list (`server.py:65`), and the official stdio I-03 test checks an unregistered commit call. This is exposure control, not authentication. `cancel_my_proposal` is a proposer mutation of a committed booking (`tools_lab.py:473`), so the broad C-03 wording about no binding mutations requires a product decision: it is not a commit but does change a booking.

Commit requires ID, revision, hash and the nested full decision, and repository comparisons use canonical bytes and check stored hash (`repos.py:510-557`); the existing stdio gate exercises idempotent retry and tampering. A compact JSON measurement with `p2-stdio-probe` and seeded IDs is 355 characters; replacing its project with 80 ASCII characters gives 421. This is a bounded demo example, not a proof for all ledger data or all JSON encoders. The implementation measures compact canonical characters at `tools_lab.py:660-668`, not the actual transport serialization or displayed card. Proposal text has no matching bound. Time fields carry absolute UTC `Z` values. Datetime parsing is tested for natural language; broader edge cases and actual human card fidelity remain unverified.

The result cap is applied after tool execution (`tools_lab.py:110-111`): an oversized mutation result may be replaced with an error after the mutation has committed, leaving the caller uncertain. Raw arbitrary input can also trigger MCP SDK validation errors before the wrapper. Profile-specific rate guards are constructed per runtime and use the injected clock (`tools_lab.py:285-298`); tests cover 30 calls and the next rejection. Default paths use platform data directories (`store/db.py:57`), though environment overrides can point elsewhere. Two concurrent MCP server processes on one ledger were not independently exercised; P1 repository race tests are not a substitute for that transport test.

Doctor separates OneDrive, key and Docker findings, and uses argument arrays for subprocesses. `request show` uses the ledger repository; tests exercise it with a path containing spaces. Doctor treats a missing ledger as informational (`cli/main.py:324-330`) without verifying whether its parent is usable, so a non-existent invalid path can be reported ready. No new regression test was written for this observation. MCP server logging is configured to stderr (`server.py:94-108`) and startup handles ledger errors (`server.py:117-132`); comprehensive malformed input, warning and exception stdout capture and startup crash-loop experiments remain UNVERIFIED.

C-01 snapshots actual tool descriptions and schemas over the official client and catch changes, but snapshot acceptance does not establish their safety. I-02 uses the official stdio client and a subprocess. `git diff 1452689 HEAD -- tests` shows substantial P1 changes as well as P2 edits; `p2-test-changes.md` explains only P2 paths. In particular the old P-05 property test is removed and a repository test replaces it (`tests/integration/test_p1_ledger.py:318`); the old SystemClock awareness assertion is replaced by a FixedClock assertion (`tests/unit/test_p1_domain.py`), while a different U-L04 test covers injected repository time. P1 evidence may explain P1 changes, but P2 evidence does not justify every modified path relative to the specified baseline. Review that history and restore or justify the lost coverage.

## P3 and P4 readiness

P3 must implement a per-server-process guard allowing at most one distinct binding commit, while allowing identical idempotent retries; register `commit_booking` with `approval_mode = "prompt"` in the effective managed session home or verified host-controlled launch layer; and ensure binding is absent unless the explicit profile and certification tuple are verified. Current required profile helps, but any caller can select `approver`, there is no process commit guard or certification check, and the server already exposes commit for that profile. An explicit profile is not a verified identity. P4 must prove actual card field fidelity, owner authorization, session-grant behavior and the installed runtime tuple; until then use proposal-only profiles. The boundary document also requires preventing session-wide approval bypass or an independently authenticated one-use token. Native approval behavior and identity are UNVERIFIED.

## Checks

Before adding the audit tests, `uv run pytest` passed 82 tests in 50.56 seconds. `uv run pytest tests/audit/test_p2_audit.py -q` then failed both new tests as intended. `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, and `uv run pyright` failed on the unrelated untracked `scripts/ops/switch_rpc.py`; this audit does not edit it. The final suite necessarily fails while the two defect tests are present. Missing and unknown profiles were exercised with `uv run lq-mcp` and `uv run lq-mcp --profile wrong`; both refused startup. No product code or existing tests were changed.
